`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` only keeps plain JSON values: Dates turn into strings, Maps and Sets become empty objects, undefined and functions vanish, and a circular reference throws. `structuredClone` keeps Dates, Maps, Sets and typed arrays and handles cycles. Neither copies functions, and `structuredClone` throws on them, while class instances come back as plain objects.

`useLayoutEffect` runs synchronously after DOM updates but before the browser paints, so use it when you measure layout (sizes, positions) and adjust it before the user sees a flash. `useEffect` runs after paint and is the right default for everything else, since layout effects block painting. Layout effects don't run on the server, so in SSR code keep them to measurement and positioning logic.

`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` loses Dates (to strings), Maps and Sets, undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. `structuredClone` keeps those types and handles cycles, and it is available in Node 18 LTS, so it's fine for the worker. Neither copies functions.

`as const` changes the inferred type: literals stay literal and everything becomes readonly, and it checks nothing. `satisfies` checks a value against a type without changing its inferred type, so typos and missing keys error but the precise type is kept. You can combine them as `as const satisfies Config`.
Action: Answer only, no code changes.

A Deployment runs interchangeable stateless pods that can be replaced in any order. A StatefulSet gives each pod a stable name and network identity, its own persistent volume (via volumeClaimTemplates) that follows it across restarts, and ordered startup and rolling updates. Pick it for databases, brokers, or anything that needs sticky identity or storage per replica.
